characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Orchestrates the creation and evaluation of non-production demonstrators to prove platform-neutral authentication paths against MitID's reliance on Apple/Google signals. It defines technical scope, selects methods (e.g., FIDO2 on GrapheneOS, or browser-based fallback), and establishes success metrics (interoperability, security, usability, and retrofit feasibility). Its objective is credible, standards-aligned evidence to inform policy, procurement language, and continuity planning, while keeping risk bounded and demonstrators non-production. Success is measured by demonstrators built, documentation of architectural requirements, and demonstrable performance gains translating into policy and procurement momentum.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Provides tangible proof points that amplify EU Standards Engagement Strategy and Procurement Influence Strategy, enabling concrete advocacy around platform neutrality. It also strengthens Policy Advocacy Strategy by grounding proposals in demonstrable evidence, and boosts Coalition Building Strategy by offering credible demonstrations that mobilize diverse stakeholders.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing on demonstrators can drive cost and schedule pressure, potentially delaying procurement wins and alienating stakeholders wary of long lead times. It may conflict with Coalition Building by privileging technical proof over inclusive engagement, and with Policy Advocacy Strategy by tilting toward technical narratives at the expense of broader privacy and governance considerations.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Orchestrates policy and regulatory engagement to translate technical feasibility into procurement-ready requirements and resilience arguments for platform neutrality. It develops position papers, lobbying plans, and formal policy proposals to Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, framing continuity of service, supplier concentration risk, procurement neutrality, and privacy governance. It coordinates messaging with the Coalition Building and EU Standards teams to shape AltID and related procurement language. Key success metrics include policy proposals submitted, formal stakeholder feedback received, and inclusion of platform-neutral and fallback requirements in official documents and procurement calls.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong positive interactions with Coalition Building and EU Standards Engagement, translating technical concepts into coalition-consensus messaging and harmonized standards ambitions. It also reinforces Procurement Influence by embedding platform-neutral and fallback requirements into procurement documents, increasing the likelihood of policy-backed vendor obligations.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Policy framing risks becoming a battleground with Technical Feasibility Strategy if demonstrators are seen as privileging certain methods, potentially undermining broad coalition goals. It may also provoke pushback from incumbent operators, constraining agility in procurement and inviting regulatory capture concerns that dilute democratic accountability.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Develops and sustains a broad, diverse coalition to advance platform neutrality and resilience objectives. It identifies and engages stakeholders across civil society, privacy advocates, academia, contingency-planning authorities, and policymakers, balancing technical credibility with democratic legitimacy. The lever structures collaboration, coordinates messaging, and builds mutual guarantees so that policy, procurement, and standards efforts gain legitimacy and momentum. It also manages expectations and trade-offs among participants, ensuring alignment on shared goals while respecting divergent priorities. Success is measured by stakeholder participation, joint position papers, formal commitments, and coordinated actions that strengthen advocacy in procurement and policy forums.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strengthens Policy Advocacy by translating diverse stakeholder input into cohesive positions, and aligns with EU Standards Engagement to mobilize broad consensus on interoperability. It also complements Technical Feasibility by ensuring that practical demonstrations reflect coalition priorities, broadening legitimacy among civil society and policymakers.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Broad coalition-building can slow decision cycles and complicate consensus, potentially conflicting with rapid procurement mandates and tight timetables. It may dilute messaging when competing priorities arise, creating tensions with Procurement Influence Strategy and Policy Advocacy Strategy if divergent coalition views stall concrete procurement language.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Coordinates the translation of policy, coalition, and technical findings into procurement language that compels vendors to adopt platform-neutral and certified fallback authentication paths. It identifies leverage points in AltID procurement, drafts concrete requirements, and negotiates with public-sector buyers to secure language that reduces dependency on Apple/Google. The lever tracks supplier diversity and risk-based scoring, with metrics such as inclusion of platform-neutral clauses in RFPs, rate of supplier diversification, and speed of adoption in procurement iterations. Ultimately, it seeks to anchor platform sovereignty in formal purchasing regimes, while remaining practical about cost and vendor capabilities.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Delivers concrete procurement language that amplifies Technical Feasibility Strategy by grounding demonstrations in purchasable requirements, and aligns with EU Standards Engagement Strategy to push interoperable, compliant specifications across jurisdictions. It also complements Policy Advocacy Strategy by translating policy positions into enforceable terms, and supports Coalition Building by offering vendor-facing commitments that stakeholders can rally behind.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Procurement-driven language risks narrowing policy debates, potentially sidelining civil-society and privacy concerns; it may conflict with Policy Advocacy Strategy if advocacy messaging seeks broader governance goals beyond procurement criteria. It could also strain Coalition Building by pushing hardline terms that alienate some stakeholders.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Directs engagement with European standards bodies and technical working groups to influence interoperability, privacy-by-design, and platform-neutral requirements within eIDAS2 and related frameworks. It translates national objectives into EU-level inputs, negotiates positions, and coordinates with other levers to ensure Danish needs are reflected in European Digital Identity Wallet materials. Its objectives include aligning Danish policy with EU direction, reducing cross-border lock-in, and shaping certified fallback concepts accepted at EU scale. Success metrics: formal EU feedback, alignment scores, and published positions in EU documents.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergizes with Policy Advocacy Strategy by channeling EU inputs into national policy proposals, and with Coalition Building by aligning cross-border standards messaging to mobilize diverse stakeholders across Denmark and Europe. It also broadens Procurement Influence by providing EU-aligned criteria that can be reflected in procurement documents and vendor evaluations.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: EU-focused engagement can dilute national urgency if EU timelines lag; it may clash with Technical Feasibility Strategy by pushing standards before demonstrators prove viability. It could also complicate Coalition Building if EU expectations create additional pressures on coalition consensus and vendor commitments.
